#Crash recovery

After Wren ends abnormally (a crash, a kill, a power cut) the next start opens the tabs again, with no setting to turn on, and never loops on a page that crashes it. browser.session.crash_recovery (on by default) is the switch; it needs browser.profile.persist (a throwaway profile writes nothing). Code: src/browser/crash_recovery.odin (decision, files, snapshot), crash_banner.odin (the bar). It is separate from browser.session.restore (reopen the tabs after a normal end, off by default).

#Files in the profile

FileMeaning
running.txtA Wren runs (or ran and ended abnormally): pid, created (the process's creation time, FILETIME) and restoring (this run reopened a crashed session and is not known stable yet). Written at the start, removed at a normal end.
recovery.txtThe snapshot: the session file format of session.odin (every tab: address, whole history tree, scroll position and zoom, which tab is current). Removed at a normal end.
crashed-session <date>.txtThe snapshot of a session that crashed twice while it was restored. The last browser.session.crash_backups are kept.

#Deciding at the start

recovery_start runs right after the single-instance step, before the window, so a start that dies early is counted too.

MarkerProcess it namesDecision
nonenormal start (a stray recovery.txt is deleted)
yesstill runs, and is not this processLive: not a crash, this start touches none of the files (no marker, no snapshot)
yes, restoring 0goneCrashed: restore recovery.txt
yes, restoring 1goneCrashed_Twice: do not restore

"Still runs" is the single-instance mutex when this process holds it (then nothing else runs on the profile and the marker is stale, even if its process id was reused), else the process id and creation time. A marker that cannot be read counts as an abnormal end. A snapshot with only blank pages is not worth restoring: the start is a plain one.

#The snapshot

recovery_touch is called where the snapshot changes (a tab opened, closed, selected or moved, a history entry added or traversed, a document parsed). It arms one timer of browser.session.crash_snapshot_ms (3 s); changes in between share one write. When it fires, the interface thread builds the text (it reads the tabs) and a worker of the blocking pool writes it atomically (temporary file, then MoveFileEx); a second write waits for the first. Nothing is written when the text did not change. At a normal end the timers stop, a write in flight finishes, then running.txt and recovery.txt are removed, the marker first (a snapshot without a marker is only stale; a marker without a snapshot would be a crash).

Reading is forgiving (session_parse_tabs): a file above 64 MiB, a tab count above browser.session.max_tabs, entries above history.tree.max_nodes per tab, addresses above browser.session.max_url_bytes or that do not parse are dropped; a truncated or foreign file restores what is readable.

#Never in a loop

A start that restores writes restoring 1 in its marker and clears it after browser.session.crash_stable_ms (30 s). If it ends before, the next start is Crashed_Twice: it moves recovery.txt to crashed-session <date>.txt, opens about:blank and shows "Wren crashed twice while restoring; your tabs are saved in ...". Restore tabs (or the command tab.restore_crashed) opens them by hand; that start is not marked restoring, so a crash after it restores the snapshot once more and the next is again Crashed_Twice: at most one restoring start in a row. Only the current tab loads at once (the others when first shown), as in browser.session.restore.

A start with an address on the command line opens the restored tabs, then the address as a new tab (shown); after two crashes the address alone.

#The bar

Wren closed unexpectedly. Restored N tabs. with Start fresh (closes the restored tabs, leaves the homepage) and Details (the newest report of <profile>\crashes written since the crashed run began, crash *.txt before unclean exit *.txt, in a tab; a notice when there is none: the process was ended from outside). The x dismisses the bar. The texts go through i18n.tr.

#Tests

odin test src/browser (crash_recovery_test.odin): marker format and every truncation, the start decision (clean, crashed, live, twice), the snapshot round trip, a truncated and a hostile file, the plan over a scratch profile (crash, restore, crash again, backup, blank page), live instance, backup pruning, report lookup, the preferences. src\tools\e2e\crash_recovery.odin (in test_all): real processes that are killed.
